newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Inmarsat in talks to enter Bulgarian market.
newsitem.headline: Inmarsat in talks to enter Bulgarian market.

text.p: London-based international communications organisation Inmarsat is in Bulgaria for talks on launching its new range of mobile satellite phones, company officials said on Tuesday.
"We are in Sofia to discuss with Bulgarian government officials the introduction of our new mobile communications services," said David Wright, Inmarsat manager for policy and regulatory issues.
Pal Horvath, Inmarsat central and eastern European director, said they had met officials in the posts and communications committee and the transport ministry.
He said Inmarsat was discussing providing communications for ships, aircraft, trucks, trains, and people whose activities took them beyond the range of conventional communications systems.
He also said he hoped Bulgaria would liberalise strict regulations governing telecommunications operators.

"Since Bulgaria joined the World Trade Organisation on December 1 they should now consider liberalising the regulations affecting international communications including satellite services to benefit Bulgaria's business," he said.

Horvath said satellite telephones could benefit anyone needing communications in remote areas not served by Bulgaria's existing mobile networks and could for example be an important communication link with the nuclear power plant at Kozloduy.
Bulgaria is working to upgrade its century-old telephone network with the addition of digital lines but the government is desperately short of cash for infrastructure investment.
